info.title: genesis-point pipeline server
info.description:
Public HTTP API for the genesis-point reconstruction control plane (photogrammetry + gaussian splatting). Upload a dataset, submit a job, stream its progress over SSE, then list and download the run's artifacts.

**Auth:** every endpoint requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` except the health/bootstrap probes. **Long-running jobs:** progress streams over SSE at `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}/stream` (resume with `Last-Event-ID`). **Downloads:** artifact/image endpoints return a `307` to a short-lived presigned URL — your HTTP client must follow redirects. **Errors:** non-2xx responses are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457): branch on `code`, quote `request_id` to support.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: One key per user action, reused for every retry of it. A replay returns the first response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

put.description:
Rename a run. Display only -- its artifacts keep the object-store prefix they were
written under, so this is safe on a finished job and on a running one alike.

delete.description: Erase a finished run: its artifacts, its log and its row. Not recoverable.

get.description:
`events` narrows the stream to a comma-separated subset of the kinds in
`_EVENT_LINE`; empty means all of them. A progress row wants `stage,progress,gpu,end`
and would otherwise be sent -- and have to drop -- the job's whole log.

delete.description: Delete one of a job's output files, leaving the rest of the run in place.

The by-run twin of `delete_artifact`: a finished run outlives the job that made it,
and the gallery addresses it by path rather than by job id.

Delete a run's outputs. The run lives in the object store (the listing and download
routes read it from `run_prefix`), so that is what has to go; the local rmtree only
covers a pre-S3 leftover, and its absence is not a 404.

get.description:
Ingest poll target. Byte progress is tracked client-side against the S3 parts, so
bytes_received here only moves at the end.

The account's spendable credit balance and platform plan. `plan_name` is the plan's
display name from the active price list (null when unknown). `billable` is false only
for the service principal, which is never charged. `credits_ok` is false when new paid
work would be refused (no credit left or a monthly spending cap reached);
`has_purchased` says whether the account has ever bought credits.

Pre-submit credit estimate: the exact number POST /jobs will hold before it runs
(same measurement, same price) and the spendable balance. `allowed` says whether that
hold would be granted now; when it is false, `reason` carries the code POST /jobs would
answer (`insufficient_credits`, `purchase_required`, `spend_cap`, `service_held`,
`service_disabled`, `account_closed`), so the client can send the user to Studio first.
404s a dataset of another account or an unknown pipeline (no leak of either).

Artifact.title: Artifact
Artifact.description:
One downloadable deliverable of a finished run. `name` is the path relative
to the run output dir (POSIX, may contain '/'); `primary` flags the model the
UI should suggest by default for this pipeline.

FieldError.description:
One rejected input. Exactly one of `pointer` (JSON body, RFC 6901), `parameter`
(query or path name) and `header` says where it is.
FieldError.title: FieldError

Problem.description:
Body of every non-2xx response (`application/problem+json`, RFC 9457). Branch on
`code`; `detail` is text for a developer. `errors` comes with `validation_failed`,
`required` and `available` with a credit refusal, `hold_reason` with `service_held`.
Problem.title: Problem

JobDatasetEvent.description:
The dataset-level deliverable of a run, once it is readable in the store.
`name` is the model subdir under datasets/{id}/sparse/ ('0_geo' when the run
geo-registered), and `url` is the endpoint that serves it.
JobDatasetEvent.title: JobDatasetEvent
